review_notes: I read the whole target file and the definitions file Definitions/Def_AutomorphicForm_GL2ConjugacyCells.lean. The simp interface is thin: all four `mem_*_iff` lemmas are `Iff.rfl` with no `@[simp]`. The target proof works around this by passing the lemmas and the raw definitions to `simp only`. I did not check other downstream users of these lemmas, so how much a `@[simp]` attribute would help elsewhere is uncertain. I saw no rewrite cycles or competing rules in this file. The finding is modest and about interface ergonomics only.

findings.problem: The cell-membership lemmas have no simp attribute and no canonical normal form. The closing steps unfold `IsUnipotentType`, `IsHyperbolicType` and `IsEllipticType` by name inside `simp only`. They also pass a locally built `hcp` and `hcen_iff` as rewrite rules. The central case has no membership rewrite at all: `mem_centralCell_iff` is missing from the `p2m_export` list, and the first conjunct is closed by `refine ⟨hcen_iff, …⟩`, which relies on the membership being defeq. Each caller therefore has to hand-pick the unfolding set. A set-level `centralCell` goal is handled differently from the other three cells.
findings.proposed_change: In the definitions file, mark `mem_centralCell_iff`, `mem_unipotentCell_iff`, `mem_hyperbolicCell_iff` and `mem_ellipticCell_iff` `@[simp]`, so membership normalises to the predicate form. Also add `mem_centralCell_iff` to the `p2m_export` list. Better, state conjugation-invariance lemmas once, such as a charpoly-based `IsHyperbolicType` iff, and tag them `@[simp]` or use them directly. Then the three bullets can use a plain `simp [hcp, hcen_iff]`, or a `rw`, instead of unfolding the definitions by name.
findings.benefit: Membership goals for all four cells would simplify the same way. Proofs would not need to know how the `Is*Type` predicates are defined. The central cell would no longer be the odd one out in the export list and in this proof.
